Israel bombed the Rafie Nia Synagogue in Tehran.

Yes, you read that right. Israel bombed a synagogue. In Iran. 

Most Americans probably didn't know that there are ~100 synagogues in Iran, 30 of which are in Tehran.

On @Bannons_WarRoom, I explain why the Iranians believe they have escalation dominance. If Trump attacks their energy infrastructure, Iran can take out the same infrastructure in the GCC. That will create a production problem that can take years to fix, and as a result, oil prices will shoot up and remain high for months, perhaps years. This will lead to a global recession, which will be devastating for Trump.

Told @Bannons_WarRoom that while the methodology of the indirect talks are problemic, the real problem lies in the substance. Trump acts as if he can dictate the terms, but reality is that Iran has significant leverage over the US in a manner it didn't before the war. Told @aje that the question is if there can be a pathway toward an agreement or if Trump continues to bomb Iran for another 2 weeks and then declares victory and leaves the Straits under Iranian control - since the fate of the Straits impacts Asian powers far more than the US.

Spoke to @democracynow about what Trump's comments about US weapons going to Kurdish groups in Iran tell us about what actually happened during the protests in which the Iranian government killed several thousand demonstrators.

Told @ABC that Trump will have a hard time getting Tehran to agree to a ceasefire with several phases, given the US and Israeli track record in Gaza and Lebanon, where Israel immediately violated the ceasefires and the latter phases were never reached.

abcnews.com/video/131778340/

Is this Israel seeking to sabotage any of the diplomacy, or is this the US signalling that Trump's deadlines are completely void of meaning and are only for show?
